channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Baltimore’s Week game against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

“We do think we will have Lamar this game,” Minter said. Jackson practiced in full on Friday and has missed the last three weeks with his high-ankle sprain. The Ravens will likely clear him from the injury report later today. Jackson told reporters that he feels like “I’m no longer a statue.” Jackson will be “safe” to use as a QB1 against the Bills in what profiles as a fantasy points bonanza.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said James Pearce Jr. (suspension) will be added back to the Falcons 53-man roster next week when eligible.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

“He’s done everything that we have asked, everything that he has been allowed to do, he’s done a great job,” Stefanski said while saying that Pearce would play in Madrid against the Bengals. Pearce was suspended after violating the league’s personal conduct policy for three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

Source: Josh Kendall

item.title: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable for Week 8 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Tytus Howard CLE Tackle

Howard returned to the practice field Friday after missing both sessions to start the week, keeping the door open for him to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday’s game against the Steelers. Howard will need to remain asymptomatic and gain clearance from an independent neurologist to play.

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Sauce Gardner (calf) will be active for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Sauce Gardner IND Cornerback

Gardner missed last week’s game after suffering a calf strain in Week 6 against the Titans, but will return after getting in a limited session on Wednesday and a full practice on Thursday. We’re assuming that means he’s in line for another full practice today.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Billy Bowman (hamstring) is questionable for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Billy Bowman ATL Cornerback

Like teammate Divine Deablo, Bowman returned to the practice field Thursday with a limited showing after missing the Week 7 win over the 49ers. The team gives him the questionable designation for Week 8 against the Buccaneers, keeping the door open for a return following one missed game. We’ll gain further clarity when the team released inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick on Sunday.

item.title: Divine Deablo (forearm) is questionable for Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Divine Deablo ATL Linebacker

Deablo returned to the practice field in limited capacity Thursday after missing the team’s Week 7 win over the 49ers, keeping the door open for a return to the active game-day roster. We’ll get our final update when the team announces their inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick on Sunday.

item.title: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Robinson will miss a second straight game with his hamstring injury, which positions Khalil Herbert to again serve as the backup to Bijan Robinson. Herbert rushed two times for nine yards in last week’s win over the 49ers while adding one reception for 19 additional yards. He will not be on the streaming radar this week.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said A.J. Brown (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

This feels like a very optimistic questionable after Brown missed the last two practices of the week with a new knee tweak. Brown-reliant managers should be making contingency plans ready for Sunday. “We’ll see when he comes in tomorrow, and we’ll make a decision,” Vrabel said.

Source: Chad Graff

item.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Steichen said Taylor will see a full workload despite being the subject of trade rumors for a Colts team that will clearly be sellers at the deadline. Taylor is healthy and not on the injury report, so this is strictly an update to inform fantasy managers they can start him with confidence this week. Taylor remains a high-end RB1 as long as his normal workload remains intact.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Tyler Warren (groin) is “good to go” for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren was limited in practice on Thursday and Wednesday and will return to a rough receiver corps against a Jaguars defense coming off bye. Warren remains a startable TE1, but it’s hard to forge much of a ceiling case for him at this point.

Source: Mike Chappell

item.title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Josh Downs will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars despite his trade request.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

Steichen confirmed that Downs did indeed request a trade, but that won’t stop him from being on the field this week against the Jaguars. The Colts appear to be in full sell mode after trading away OG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner earlier this week. Downs has been on the practice field this week and profiles as a fringe WR3/WR4 after a string of tough outings.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Antoine Winfield Jr. will return in Week 8 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Antoine Winfield TB Safety

Winfield has missed the last three games due to fractured ribs he suffered in Week 4. Winfield has earned a 76.8 defensive grade per PFF this season while racking up 24 tackles. The Panthers’ secondary held up fairly well during his three-game absence, allowing only 235.0 passing yards per game, but his return will be a welcomed one for Bowles and his defense.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Emeka Egbuka (foot) will not play in Week 8 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Bowles said Egbuka did clear concussion protocol, but the foot injury he has been dealing with for the last two weeks will officially sideline him for this week’s game against the Falcons. Hopefully this isn’t any kind of a major setback for Egbuka, who shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday’s practice and was limited in the first two practices to start the week. Ted Hurst will again operate as the Buccaneers’ primary outside target but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a risky WR4.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

After being a DNP in each of the Eagles’ first two practices of the week, it’s far too early to be confident that Barkley will suit up on Sunday night against the Commanders. That said, his return to the field is still an encouraging sign for the Eagles, whose backfield is suddenly among the most banged up in the league. We will check back in when the Eagles announce Barkley’s Week 8 status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this ends up being a game-time decision, which could prove frustrating for fantasy managers. We should know more on his availability in the next few hours.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: A.J. Brown (knee) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown has now missed back-to-back practices and is at serious risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Dolphins. Brown’s knee injury was reported as a “flare-up” from a previous knee injury, which is never a good sign for a player. Brown has been dealing with injuries like this for a few years but has always found a way to play through them. While it’s possible he ends up doing so again this week, fantasy managers should begin considering other options in the event he is held out.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Tate was a DNP all week and is at risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Bengals. The team will announce his official status shortly, but if he is unable to go, Wan’Dale Robinson and Elic Ayomanor would be the early favorites to see an uptick in targets against a Bengals secondary that ranks 18th in points allowed to opposing receivers this season.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

After being limited in back-to-back practices to start the week, and shedding his non-contact jersey on Thursday, Egbuka being a DNP on Friday is a notable setback. Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman speculated that Egbuka will “be ruled out again” for Week 8’s game against the Falcons, but we’ll wait for official word from the team before drawing conclusions. That said, the Bucs could again have Ted Hurst operating as their primary outside threat.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Baker Mayfield was seen without his protective glove during Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield wore the protective glove during last week’s game to avoid further damage to the thumb he injured in Week 3. Mayfield attempted only 11 passes in his return against the Panthers last week, but that was all he needed in a game where the Buccaneers totaled over 250 yards on the ground. Hopefully the shedding of his protective glove is a sign that he’s no longer at risk of re-injury heading into Week 8’s game against the Falcons.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Panthers named DL coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator.
item.description:
Todd Wash CAR Coaching Staff

Wash will take over for the now-departed Ejiro Evero, who was dismissed shortly after the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers. Wash, who has been with the Panthers since 2023, spent five seasons as the Jaguars’ defensive coordinator (2016 to 2020), with his defense finishing top five in both yards and points allowed in 2017 and 2018. Wash’s first task will be finding ways to improve a run defense that ranks among the worst in the league through the first half of the season, but given that his fingerprints are all over the defensive line, it’s hard to imagine a noticeable improvement is on the way over the final 10 weeks of the season.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be limited in Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

This will be the third straight limited practice for Hall, which is an encouraging sign as he looks to return to action since last playing in Week 3 against the Lions. If he’s active, Hall will likely find himself in a bit more of a timeshare with Braelon Allen, who has rushed for 357 yards and a touchdown on 72 carries in Hall’s absence while averaging a solid 5.0 YPC. We will provide an update on Hall’s Week 8 availability when the team announces it, but at worst, we would expect him to carry a questionable tag entering the weekend.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Panthers fired DC Ejiro Evero.
item.description:
Ejiro Evero

Just hours after a 27-19 loss to the Packers that saw the Panthers fall below .500 for the first time this season, the team has decided to part ways with Evero after nearly four full seasons with the team. Evero was a holdover from Frank Reich’s 2023 staff and drew a handful of head coaching interviews during the last hiring cycle after his defense finished 15th in points allowed and 16th in yards allowed. The Panthers’ best defensive performances of the season came in games where Cooper Rush and Tanner McKee made starts, but they’ve allowed 35.2 points per game when facing opposing teams’ QB1s this season. From 2022 to 2023, Evero’s defenses ranked seventh and fourth in yards allowed per game, but his units have struggled in more recent seasons. They have particularly struggled on the ground and rank near the bottom of the league in rushing yards allowed and YPC allowed, while allowing a league-high 12 rushing touchdowns. He’ll likely get another job in a coaching role next offseason, in hopes of earning another coordinator job over the next few seasons.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young’s knee injury may be limiting his mobility.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Young declined to get into details about his knee injury after Thursday night’s loss to the Packers, saying, “Everyone’s dealing with something; it’s no excuse,” when speaking with the media after the game. Canales didn’t seem overly concerned about Young’s injury after the game, but did acknowledge that he didn’t appear to have the “quick, make you miss” aspect to his game against the Packers. Young was listed on the Panthers’ injury report throughout the week, but was also a full participant in practice. Young’s knee could be partly to blame for the six sacks he took in Thursday’s loss, and his health will be one to monitor in the weeks ahead, especially with the team already past its Week 5 bye. Assuming he’s good to go in Week 9, Young will face an uphill battle against a stout Broncos defense.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-6 targets for 53 yards with a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Kraft was able to bring in a score between a pair of defenders to give the Pack a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. That’s back-to-back games for the tight end with a score, and three in the first half of 2026. Kraft has seen a similar amount of involvement throughout the campaign, and he’ll likely put up a similar statline — hopefully with a touchdown for fantasy managers who roster him — in Week 9 versus the Patriots.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Matthew Golden caught 7-of-13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden is rarely boring, that’s for sure. He dropped two passes, and one of those was a wide-open touchdown in the second quarter. The good news for Golden, Jordan Love and fantasy managers was that he was wide open again on the next play, and he was able to bring that pass in. Golden’s athleticism and ability to get down field is unquestionable, but to say the efficiency isn’t there is an understatement. He’ll be back at it in Week 9 against the Patriots.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker’s fumble came on the last play of the game as the Panthers played pitchy woo woo in their attempt to tie the game. The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Tetairoa McMillan CAR Wide Receiver

McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Chuba Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers, adding seven receptions for 38 yards.
item.description:
Chuba Hubbard CAR Running Back

Hubbard was easily the most effective offensive player for the Panthers, but that’s at least partially an insult to everyone else as much as it was compliment to him. The tailback was able to make the most of the limited rushing room, and with Bryce Young having zero time to throw the football, he was a frequent target of Young’s checkdowns. Trevor Etienne received just one carry for one yard, meanwhile. Hubbard’s usage makes him a high-end RB2 for Week 9 against the Broncos, even if it’s more floor than ceiling.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Josh Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers, adding six catches for 13 yards and another score.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs’ fantasy game was salvaged with two scores, but the tailback didn’t look particularly spry in the process. He had a long gain of just six, and there was almost no burst even against the porous Panthers’ run defense. He was involved in the passing game, but again, outside of his four-yard receiving score, there really wasn’t much there. It’s clear this is Jacobs’ backfield despite the scuffles, as MarShawn Lloyd had just three touches in the contest for seven yards. He’s a volatile low-end RB1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jordan Love completed 30-of-41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception in the Packers’ 27-19, Week 8 win over the Panthers.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Love completed 17 of his first 20 passes, and two of those incompletions were drops. He threw a seed to Tucker Kraft for his first touchdown between defenders, found Matthew Golden wide open in the end zone for his second score — one play after Golden dropped a touchdown — and connected with Josh Jacobs for his third score of the day. The interception was a heinous decision where he didn’t see the safety, but outside of that, it was an impressive evening for the 27-year-old. Love gets zero, well, love from the run game and doesn’t have a quality offensive line, but he’s still putting up respectable numbers. He’ll look to add to those numbers in Week 9 against the Patriots in what should be a fun matchup.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

Source: Rob Demovsky

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jack Bech (forearm) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jack Bech LV Wide Receiver

That’s back-to-back full practices for Bech after the Raiders opened up the 21-day window for the wideout. He’s worth monitoring in redraft leagues in part because the options ahead of him aren’t exactly elite, but fantasy managers don’t need to consider a stash just yet.

Source: Adam Kaplan

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price gets in the limited session after coach Mike Macdonald said that it was realistic that the tailback could be back Monday night against the Bears in Week 8. Zach Charbonnet was a full participant Thursday, so the Seattle backfield could finally be at full strength — or close to it, anyway — for the stretch. That’s nice for the Seahawks, but creates a lot of confusion from a fantasy perspective.

Source: Gregg Bell

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed received positive news on his knee injury that caused him to leave Sunday’s blowout win over the Chiefs, but there’s a pretty good chance that he’s going to miss at least Week 8’s game against Chicago on Monday. Assuming that’s the case, it will lead to more snaps for Tory Horton both as a receiver and as the primary returner.

Source: Gregg Bell

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 8. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

Source: Gregg Bell

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue his recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

item.title: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Tre' Harris LAC Wide Receiver

Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

item.title: RJ Harvey (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday after being limited in practice due to a knee injury, something fantasy managers will want to monitor as the weekend approaches. Either way, Harvey now has two healthy backs to compete with for touches with the return of Jonah Coleman in Week 7, keeping him on the fringes of FLEX consideration entering a difficult matchup against the Chiefs.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

item.title: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practiced in full Thursday.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Diggs shook of the absence Wednesday with a full showing Thursday, indicating he is tracking well to suit up when the Commanders face off against the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. The tam previously indicated that Diggs’ modest role would not grow in the absence of Terry McLaurin, potentially paving the way for rookie Antonio Williams to see an increase in role and opportunity in the second half of the season. Fantasy managers will want to confirm Diggs’ status on the final injury report Friday, but it appears as if he will be available in Week 8.

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in practice Thursday.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

It’s the second consecutive limited showing for the co-alpha receiver, who will likely need to upgrade to a full showing on Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend. Pickens has played through the shoulder issue for two weeks, but the hamstring ailment is worth monitoring as the weekend approaches. Pickens is a viable WR2 in a solid matchup against the Cardinals, if active.

item.title: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in practice Thursday.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

It was the second consecutive day in which Wilson practiced with a yellow non-contact jersey after stating Wednesday that the team was simply being overly cautious. Wilson appears on track to maintain a high-volume role in the pass-heavy Cardinals offense in Week 8 against the Cowboys, where he will be a borderline WR1, if active.

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

The consecutive limited showings seems to indicate Moore is on track to return from a two-game absence, something we should get further fidelity on after Friday’s practice. There remains a possibility that Moore carries a questionable designation into the weekend if he is unable to upgrade to a full participant Friday, leaving fantasy managers hopeful yet uncertain as we near the weekend. Moore would return to a WR2 profile when the Bills take on the Ravens, if active.

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase quickly puts his fantasy managers’ worries to rest, returning to a full session Thursday after being limited Wednesday. The Bengals will be playing without two tight ends and their WR3 in Andre Iosivas, but their primary contributors remain one of the healthier units as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Chase can be started as a top tier WR1 against the Titans.

item.title: Braelon Allen (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Braelon Allen NYJ Running Back

It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday limited session. We’re pretty sure Allen will play this week and was just being managed on Wednesday, but how often he’ll be playing will depend on how Breece Hall’s situation shakes out on Friday.

item.title: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Hall appears more likely than not to play this week if he can get in one more practice on Friday. At the very least, he’s likely headed for an actual questionable tag this week. We’ll see what Aaron Glenn has to say Friday morning. Braelon Allen-reliant managers will want to pay attention to that one.

item.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai has yet to practice after sustaining thumb and toe injuries in Week 4, with the potential that he misses his fourth consecutive game a very real possibility. The Bears held a walkthrough Thursday ahead of a Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks, meaning Monangai will have two more opportunities to get on the practice field ahead of Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best making alternate arrangements considering the timing of the team’s game.

item.title: Greg Dulcich (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Greg Dulcich MIA Tight End

Still, back-to-back practices are a good sign that Dulcich will be ready to go for Week 8’s game against the Patriots. That isn’t necessarily an endorsement of using him in fantasy football — even after last week’s surprise 5/86 against the Jets — but hey, the Dolphins will be glad he’s around.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) practiced in full Thursday.
item.description:
Jahmyr Gibbs DET Running Back

The return to practice comes on the heels of a missed practice Wednesday for the veteran workhorse, immediately putting fantasy managers at ease for Week 8. Managers will want to confirm his practice status Friday before making final preparations for the weekend, but it certainly appears as if Gibbs will be good to go for a normal, and massive, workload when the Lions take the field against the division rival Vikings.

item.title: Malik Washington (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Malik Washington MIA Wide Receiver

Back-to-back limited sessions probably leave Washington in a good spot for Week 8. He’s more likely than not to be cleared off the injury report on Friday as long as there’s not a sudden downgrade.

item.title: Jalen Coker caught 2-of-5 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers while also losing a fumble.
item.description:
Jalen Coker CAR Wide Receiver

Coker’s fumble came on the last play of the game as the Panthers played pitchy woo woo in their attempt to tie the game. The 24-year-old didn’t have a catch in the first half, but salvaged his fantasy day — to a point, anyway — with a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young. The 24-year-old has just three catches over the last two games, and he’ll try and get things going against the Broncos in Week 9.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-11 targets for 57 yards in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Tetairoa McMillan CAR Wide Receiver

McMillan had a long gain of just 14 yards, as Bryce Young just didn’t have time to get the ball down the field and wasn’t particularly accurate on the rare times he did. The wideout was targeted early and often, but it was an inefficient effort for the 23-year-old, at best. Even as the clear top option in this passing attack — all due respect to Jalen Coker — there’s a ton of volatility in McMillan’s fantasy profile, and that won’t change for Week 9 against the Broncos.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Chuba Hubbard rushed 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 8 loss to the Packers, adding five receptions for 38 yards.
item.description:
Chuba Hubbard CAR Running Back

Hubbard was easily the most effective offensive player for the Panthers, but that’s at least partially an insult to everyone else as much as it was compliment to him. The tailback was able to make the most of the limited rushing room, and with Bryce Young having zero time to throw the football, he was a frequent target of Young’s checkdowns. Trevor Etienne received just one carry for one yard, meanwhile. Hubbard’s usage makes him a high-end RB2 for Week 9 against the Broncos, even if it’s more floor than ceiling.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interceptions in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 9. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

Source: Gregg Bell

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tyler Allgeier (toe) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

Allgeier was able to get a bump up after a DNP for Wednesday. It appears to just be a case of rest for the 26-year-old, but fantasy managers who will consider Allgeier for Week 8 against the Cowboys if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) can’t go — Love was also limited Thursday — should keep an eye on Friday’s designation.

Source: Adam Kaplan

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was listed as a limited participate in practice Thursday.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

That’s a second straight limited session for Love. The Cardinals are taking this slowly with the 21-year-old ahead of a potential return in Week 8 against the Cowboys, but fantasy managers will obviously need to pay close attention to how much he practices Friday and his injury designation.

Source: Adam Kaplan

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, OLB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, G Damien Lewis, G Torricelli Simpkins, and DT Bobby Brown inactive for Week 8 against the Packers.
item.description:
Ja'Tavion Sanders CAR Tight End

The Panthers are extremely shorthanded along the offensive line and on the defensive side of the ball, most notably in the secondary and with the pass rush. That could spell trouble agains the high-powered Green Bay passing game, particularly with wide receiver Matthew Golden active. The Panthers look to halt their recent skid on the road in hostile territory at Lambeau Field.

item.title: Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is active for Week 8 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden got in a lone limited session in preparation for the team’s Week 8 meeting with the Panthers on a short week, ultimately able to go as he looks to continue to recent hot stretch in fantasy production. No limitation in expected role has been passed by the team, meaning Golden should be good to go for a normal workload against the Panthers. Fantasy managers can confidently insert him into Week 8 rosters as an upside WR2. Inactive for the Packers are TE Jonnu Smith, RB Kaleb Johnson, LB Zaire Franklin, G Donovan Jennings, C Sean Rhyan, and G Travis Glover.

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Illnesses typically don’t hold back NFL players, so we’d be surprised if Henderson missed time, but it is worth noting that it was a Thursday addition to the report. Because of that, if he missed Friday, it wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed as questionable. We’d still expect him to play either way.

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

The upgrade from “DNP” to a full session indicates St. Brown will be fine for a normal workload when the Lions face off against the Vikings Sunday, easing fantasy managers’ collective minds after the star receiver was not present at practice Wednesday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on Friday’s injury report, but it certainly appears as if the team will have their veteran alpha for the divisional tilt.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers has put together a pair of limited sessions out of the bye and seems likely to play against the Colts in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr.'s disappearing act has left Meyers capable of putting up WR3 lines, but the Colts may not be opponent enough to force that kind of production out of Meyers this week.

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Colts have told teams they won’t move Adetomiwa Adebawore.
item.description:
Adetomiwa Adebawore IND Defensive Tackle

Adebawore, a fourth-round pick in 2023, played under 200 snaps in each of his first two seasons and was a pass-rush specialist in 2025. In 2026, he’s taken a step forward, with an 81.8 PFF grade buoyed by an 86.3 pass rush grade. It would be reasonable to expect the Colts to try to extend a player like this, but they sure didn’t seem to have any urgency to do it before the year.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

It was his second consecutive limited showing following two missed games, with his level of activity Friday likely to be telling as it pertains to a potential return in Week 8. Warren’s absence has been felt hard by a Colts offense that has struggled to move the football consistently. He would likely return to a sizable role over the middle of the field against the pass-funnel Jaguars, if active in Week 8.

item.title: Aaron Jones (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones was forced from the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts due to an aggravation of an existing knee injury. The fact he was able to return to the practice field in any capacity after missing Wednesday’s session is good news for his potential availability against the Lions. We would expect him to form a loose committee with Jordan Mason, if active Sunday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his level of participation Friday.

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

He played last week just fine, so it seems like he was just given a bit of a breather on Wednesday during a limited session. Sampson should handle 5-10 touches for the Browns on Sunday against the Steelers.

item.title: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

He hasn’t practiced since before Week 6 and looks likely to be ruled out again on Friday. Khalil Herbert ran in Robinson’s place as the backup last week and would handle those duties again against Tampa on Sunday if Robinson is ruled out.

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said it’s “realistic” that Jadarian Price (chest/IR) could return in Week 8.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

With Zach Charbonnet’s status also in some doubt, Seattle’s backfield situation likely won’t be sorted out until Saturday (or MNF inactives), but if Price is back that’s probably the end of Emmanuel Wilson’s short-term RB2 ride. We’ll keep an eye on the situation. Wilson-reliant managers might want to consider alternative arrangements for Week 8.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Chiefs special teams coach Dave Toub said Harrison Butker is “our kicker.”
item.description:
Harrison Butker KC Kicker

“He went 10-for-10 yesterday, with Justin Tucker right there. ... We’re going to keep working it,” Toub continued. It sounds like despite signing Tucker, Butker will continue to kick for the Chiefs. At least this week, anyway.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) was present at practice Thursday.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

That now marks consecutive days on the practice field for the veteran receiver whom has missed the previous two games. The Chiefs also had their bye in Week 5, giving Rice a full three weeks of recovery, which combines with his recent practice availability to make it likely he returns to face the Broncos. The Chiefs managed just 25 combined points in the two games without Rice.

item.title: Mansoor Delane (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Mansoor Delane KC Cornerback

Delane’s absence raises concerns surrounding his potential availability when the Broncos in Week 8. Coming off their first loss of the season, the Chiefs will look to rebound against a divisional opponent after managing only three points against the Seahawks. Delane has been a big part of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s weekly game plan, allowing the team to rank near the top of the league in man coverage rate through the first third of the season.

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks has not practiced since before Week 6’s loss to the Panthers and should be seen as doubtful heading into Friday’s practice session. We’d be surprised if he played in Week 8.

Source: Olivia Reiner

item.title: DeVonta Smith was not spotted at practice on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Assuming there’s not a non-media practice portion that adds him to the report, Smith will enter Friday as fairly unlikely to play. We’ll see if he can get on the practice field on Friday. A limited session might get him on to the questionable line. Smith last practiced ahead of Week 6.

Source: Olivia Reiner

item.title: A.J. Brown (knee) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

The downgrade in participation raises serious questions surrounding his potential availability when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Brown had been mostly limited in practice since being activated from injured reserve due to a separate ankle issue, with the absence Thursday marking the first fully missed practice in that window. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status Friday as they make plans for their weekend ahead. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Thursday that the veteran receiver’s absence is due to a “flare up” of a previous knee injury, placing his status for Sunday in doubt.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

This doesn’t look ideal. Barkley practiced all week leading up to his return, and at this point he doesn’t even have a limited session ahead of Sunday’s game with the Commanders. There’s probably not a zero percent chance that Barkley is playing, but at this point the best Barkley-reliant managers can likely hope for is a questionable tag on Friday. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue would be in line to form some sort of committee if Barkley can’t go.

Source: Olivia Reiner

item.title: Keisean Nixon (shoulder) is questionable for Thursday Night Football against the Panthers.
item.description:
Keisean Nixon GB Cornerback

Nixon was added to the injury report Thursday with a shoulder injury and is now listed questionable for Week 8 against the Panthers. We’ll get his final determination 90-minutes prior to first kick.

item.title: Divine Deablo (forearm) and Billy Bowman (hamstring) returned to practice Thursday.
item.description:
Divine Deablo ATL Linebacker

Both players missed the team’s Week 7 win over the 49ers before starting Week 8 preparations with absences. A return to the practice field Thursday keeps the possibility of returns open ahead of a matchup against the Buccaneers.

item.title: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) missed practice Thursday.
item.description:
Jaylinn Hawkins BAL Safety

Hawkins was absent for the second consecutive day, requiring some level of participation Friday to avoid a designation for the team’s showdown against the Bills in Week 8. The team got good news on other fronts as Lamar Jackson, Ioane Vega, Kyle Hamilton, and Roquan Smith were all present Thursday.

item.title: Bucky Irving (rest) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

Irving was absent from Thursday’s sessions with an official “rest” designation, allowing fantasy managers to breath a collective sigh of relief after the veteran back has morphed into a borderline workhorse in recent games. Managers can likely continue forward with Irving in their starting lineups as an upside RB2 against the Falcons.

item.title: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
item.description:
Roquan Smith BAL Linebacker

Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

It’s the second consecutive full practice for Jackson, who is attempting to return from a three-game absence to face the Bills in Week 8. The two full sessions were also his first such practices since injuring his ankle, a positive development toward an active status in a marquee matchup. He’ll have one more opportunity to maintain his level of participation, which would likely keep him off the injury report heading into the weekend.

item.title: Elgton Jenkins and Jared Verse practiced Thursday.
item.description:
Elgton Jenkins CLE Offensive Lineman

Both players emerged from their Week 7 win a bit banged up, with their return to practice Thursday a positive development toward an active game-day status. Right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) remained sidelined, who will have one more opportunity to get on the practice field and remain asymptomatic to have a chance at playing against the Steelers in Week 8.

item.title: Kyle Hamilton (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
item.description:
Kyle Hamilton BAL Safety

Hamilton was seen in full pads, participating in practice the day after being held out due to a knee injury. The All Pro safety-linebacker hybrid is arguably the most important piece of the Baltimore defense considering his absurd flexibility to play multiple positions on the field. While the official status of his return has not been provided by the team, it’s a step in the right direction ahead of a divisional showdown against the Bills in Week 8.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

Source: Terry McCormick

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

Tate has now missed two practices with the shoulder issue, making him truly questionable for Sunday’s game versus the Bengals. Tate has been operating as the Titans’ clear WR1, meaning there would be plenty of opportunities up for grabs if he can’t go. Wan’Dale Robinson could be in line for more targets, but his slot-only role doesn’t have much overlap with Tate’s job. Second-year wideout Elic Ayomanor might be the best bet to see more work if Tate is out this week, though that would only move him into the WR4 ranks.

Source: Terry McCormick

item.title: Colts signed OT Charlie Heck, formerly of the Dolphins.
item.description:
Charlie Heck IND Tackle

Heck spent the offseason with the Dolphins but did not make their final roster. He has 29 career starts, with all but two of them coming at right tackle. His most recent action came in Tampa Bay, where he started six games in 2025.

item.title: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) shed his non-contact jersey for Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

There’s a good chance Egbuka has been upgraded to a full participant in practice, meaning he is making his way through the league’s concussion protocol. He remains on track to play this week after missing Week 7. With Baker Mayfield back under center, Egbuka may be able to turn around his season after a rather quiet start to the year. He is in the WR2 mix for Week 8 versus the Falcons.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) returned to practice Thursday.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell missed Wednesday’s session with the hip issue. He will likely be listed as limited today, but that still puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Falcons. Gainwell racked up 14 carries in a blowout win over the Panthers last week, but that hasn’t been the norm for him. Gainwell is averaging 6.4 touches per game and has topped out at three receptions in a week. He is buried in the RB4 ranks for Week 8.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ja’Marr Chase’s ankle injury “is not considered a major deal.”
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Rap isn’t breaking much news here. Chase didn’t practice on Wednesday, but the Bengals listed him as getting a rest day on top of the ankle issue. It was just a maintenance day for one of the league’s best wideouts. Chase remains in the WR1 overall mix for his Week 8 game against the Titans.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Eagles signed RB Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to the active roster.
item.description:
Jaydon Blue PHI Running Back

Blue was called up as the replacement for Dameon Pierce, who was placed on injured reserve this week. Saquon Barkley entered Week 7 with a lingering hamstring issue. He then suffered a back injury and was in and out of the lineup for the remainder of the game. With little left to play for, the Eagles may choose to put their star running back on ice for a while. That would leave Blue and Elijah Mitchell as the next men up. Mitchell was the RB3 for Philly in Monday’s game, but he wasn’t signed to the active roster. Our money is on Blue seeing more work this week, though it’s a messy situation at best.

item.title: Bears acquired DT Jeffery Simmons and a fifth-round pick from the Titans in exchange for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick.
item.description:
Jeffery Simmons CHI Defensive Tackle

The Titans’ fourth-round pick is in 2027 and the fifth-round pick heading back to Chicago is in 2028. It’s a massive haul for a Titans team that is once again staring down the barrel of a lost season. Simmons has been the subject of trade rumors for a while, but an offseason extension quieted the murmurs this year. Tennessee inked him to a three-year, $106 million extension in June. Simmons has consistently been one of the league’s best interior pass-rushers. He racked up a career-high 11 sacks last year and already has four to his name in 2026. Though the Titans clearly wanted Simmons to be around for years to come, they couldn’t pass on the chance to hoard draft picks as they prepare for another rebuild. With Caleb Williams healthy and playing at an elite level, the Bears are going all in on this current window. They currently rank 14th in EPA per play allowed, a mark that will certainly improve in the coming weeks.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

Golden was estimated as a DNP for two walkthroughs this week before being limited in the Packers’ only real session. The short turnaround to Thursday Night Football likely forced the Packers to take an extra cautious approach with him in practice. While he almost certainly isn’t at 100 percent, Golden looks like a good bet to play in a sneaky shootout with the Panthers tonight. He will be on the WR1/2 border if he gets the green light.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson was on the practice field wearing a non-contact jersey on Wednesday. He is dealing with a rib injury, presumably suffered in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos. He will be limited as long as he wears the non-contact jersey and ideally finishes the week without it in order to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Kendrick Bourne suddenly becomes the WR1 if Wilson cannot go.

item.title: Tyler Allgeier (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

Allgeier popped up on the injury report with a toe issue as rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) returned to practice in a limited fashion. Though we don’t know the severity of Allgeier’s injury, it may be worth keeping Bam Knight rostered despite Love’s return. If Allgeier cannot play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Knight will get another week of fantasy viability.

item.title: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
item.description:
Jihaad Campbell PHI Linebacker

Campbell came out of the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys dealing with hamstring and quad injuries. He starts out the week as an estimated DNP. Campbell will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play Week 8 against the Commanders.

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were estimated DNPs for the Eagles’ walkthrough. Both players missed Week 7 against the Cowboys and start off on the wrong side of questionable to open Week 8. Smith and Wicks will need to at least get a limited practice session in before they can be considered as potential fantasy options against the Commanders. With Britain Covey (knee) also DNP, the receiving corps is sparse. If neither can go, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown get a boost from the WR group while TE Dallas Goedert becomes the No. 1 pass-catcher in the Eagles offense.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley was predictably a non-participant after re-aggravating his hamstring injury and additionally injuring his back in Week 7 against the Cowboys. Despite the injuries, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Barkley said his hamstring “came out great” and he doesn’t believe his back will keep him out. With every other Eagles running back suffering long-term injuries, Barkley is attempting to gut out his injury issues. Given his re-aggravation last week, it is well within the range of outcomes for Barkley to see limited snaps in Week 8 against the Commanders. His motivation to play makes us think he is on track to be active on Sunday but Barkley is a risky RB2 as he deals with injuries.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Javon Kinlaw (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Javon Kinlaw WAS Defensive Tackle

Kinlaw is dealing with a knee issue. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday it will “likely be tough” for the 29-year-old defensive tackle to play Sunday. We can expect Kinlaw to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8 against the Eagles.

item.title: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring/rest) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Stefon Diggs WAS Wide Receiver

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn already said Diggs won’t practice Wednesday, so this is not a surprise. Quinn also confirmed the veteran will return to practice Thursday and the additional rest designation should stave off concerns of Diggs dealing with a long-term injury. He should be in the WR3/FLEX mix for Week 8 against the Eagles. Also not practicing for the Commanders was TE John Bates (shoulder).

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks was limited due to a foot injury; this is notable with the Commanders coming out of a bye week. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Burks has the opportunity to earn an increased role in the receiving corps. Fantasy managers don’t need to roster the 26-year-old yet, but Dyami Brown and Antonio Williams could see a boost in targets if Burks sits out Week 8 against the Eagles.

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new. He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status. Meanwhile, WR/KR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was an estimated DNP in practice after not playing last week. The Cowboys may be missing Turpin again as a kick returner and gadget player on offense, but Pickens should still be the WR2 for Sunday against the Cardinals.

item.title: Jalen Carter said he “probably won’t be 100-percent this year” due to a wrist injury.
item.description:
Jalen Carter PHI Defensive Tackle

Carter has been dealing with a wrist injury since the beginning of the season, playing through it for the last seven weeks. He will continue to play through it, though the Eagles defensive tackle admits the wrist won’t be fully healed this season.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Titans claimed Jonah Laulu off waivers from the Raiders.
item.description:
Jonah Laulu TEN Defensive Tackle

Tennessee waived Timmy Horne in a corresponding move. Laulu appeared in five games for the Raiders this year and recorded .5 sacks plus three QB hits. He made 15 starts for the Raiders last year and appeared in all 17 games. Laulu will be a depth option for the Titans.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Pat Surtain (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Pat Surtain DEN Cornerback

Surtain is now on track to make his return after missing multiple games with an ankle injury. The good news comes at the right time, with a bout against the division-rival Chiefs upcoming this weekend.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle’s status for Week 8 against the Chiefs has not been determined. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver aggravated his preexisting chest injury in Week 7 against the Cardinals. Backup plans should be made at this time.

Source: Chris Tomasson

item.title: Spencer Brown (back) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Spencer Brown BUF Tackle

Brown initially suffered the back injury in Week 5. He missed most of that game but was back on the field for Week 6. Coming out of the bye with a DNP today suggests the issue isn’t getting better. If Brown isn’t able to play this week, Tylan Grable will take his spot at right tackle.

item.title: Texans claimed Emari Demercado, formerly of the Cowboys, off waivers.
item.description:
Emari Demercado HOU Running Back

Demercado will need to contribute on special teams to be active on game day, and he might also need David Montgomery (groin) to remain sidelined after the Week 8 bye. Demercado does not need to be added in 12-team leagues.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid briefly left the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders with this injury, though it was called a rib issue at the time. He returned to the contest in the fourth quarter. Buffalo then got a well-timed Week 7 bye. A limited session today is nothing out of the ordinary for Kincaid. We fully expect him to play in Week 8 against the Ravens. In what could be the best game environment of the week, Kincaid remains a solid TE1 option.

item.title: Roquan Smith (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Roquan Smith BAL Linebacker

Smith was one of several Ravens defenders to miss today’s session, though we’re expecting some of them to get back on the field later in the week. Smith has one interception, one forced fumble, and two sacks across seven games this year. We’re already expecting a shootout between the Ravens and Bills on Sunday, but Smith missing the contest would certainly increase the odds of fireworks on offense.

item.title: Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ben Skowronek PIT Wide Receiver

Skowronek is not fantasy-relevant and should not be picked up in 12-team formats. His potential return provides Aaron Rodgers with a trusted target. Skowronek also serves as a reliable run blocker.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Kyle Hamilton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Kyle Hamilton BAL Safety

Neither did fellow Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is also dealing with a knee injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said a few of his players were dealing with “after game type things” when asked about Hamilton, so it doesn’t sound like this is a major issue. Still, with multiple members of the secondary banged up, this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

The Browns’ No. 2 running back played through his knee injury effectively last week, totaling 79 scrimmage yards and three receptions against the Titans. He should be expected to continue playing productively on his limited workload moving forward. He is not a must-start player in Week 8 against the Steelers, but he belongs in the FLEX conversation.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Trent McDuffie (groin) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

This is McDuffie’s first practice since he injured his groin during a Week 6 practice. He will be limited on the official injury report. Rams LB Nate Landman (concussion) will be listed as a full participant.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

It’s Jackson’s first full practice since suffering the ankle injury in Week 4. Even with the many twists and turns in this latest injury saga, we’re comfortable assuming Jackson will play this week. The fact that he was held out this long hopefully means that he’s close to 100 percent healthy. Facing a likely shootout with the Bills, Jackson projects for the second-most fantasy points at his position, behind only Josh Allen.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson has meaningfully contributed to the Rams’ offense in each of the last two weeks, but he is now at risk of missing his team’s Week 8 game against the Chargers. Were Parkinson to sit out on Sunday, Tyler Higbee would likely benefit.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Eagles placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve.
item.description:
Dameon Pierce PHI Running Back

Jaydon Blue was signed from their practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move. Pierce went down with an injury on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter of Monday’s game. The team has not announced the exact injury yet, but Pierce will now miss a minimum of four games. Blue will back up a still-very-injured Saquon Barkley. Barkley returned from his hamstring injury in Week 7, only to suffer a back injury in the process. Blue has an outside chance at starting for the Eagles this week, making him worth a look on waivers.

item.title: Carson Beck (back) will be limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback has been dealing with back spasms in recent weeks, likely delaying his rookie season debut. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Beck threw the ball well on Tuesday. Today, they will see how things go. Stay tuned.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: Walter Nolen (ankle) will not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Walter Nolen ARI Defensive Lineman

Nolen did not play in Week 7 against the Broncos. Were he to miss this week’s game against the Cowboys, his absence would only further insulate this game as a fantasy-friendly environment. The Cardinals’ permissive defense is a unit to target via matchups.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: 49ers released Jack Jones.
item.description:
Jack Jones

Jones was released to create room on the roster for DeForest Buckner, whom the 49ers just acquired from Indianapolis. Jones hasn’t played much this year, but he has been active in all seven games and sees some work on special teams. He started 17 games for the Dolphins in 2025 and 16 games for the Raiders in 2024. He shouldn’t have any issues finding a new team.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Dolphins claimed Christian Haynes off waivers from the Seahawks.
item.description:
Christian Haynes MIA Guard

It was initially reported that the Ravens claimed Haynes off waivers. The Dolphins, however, also claimed him. A worse record than the Ravens gave Miami a higher priority on waivers and they were awarded Haynes. The former third-round pick will be a useful depth option for the Dolphins.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) successfully underwent surgery, and his return timeline is “probably closer” to the shorter end of the expected 6-10 week timeline.
item.description:
Davante Adams

If Adams hit the absolute soonest return date, week-wise, he theoretically could face the Chiefs in Week 13, but that game takes place on Thursday night. We suspect facing the 49ers in Week 14 is more likely, though nothing is guaranteed for a 33-year-old player. Adams should be stashed in injured reserve spots, where possible. He makes for a tough cut in leagues without them.

Source: Stu Jackson

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported last week that Ferguson’s return was still going to take “some time.” That doesn’t make it sound like he’s awfully close to getting back on the field. Tyler Higbee leads the Rams’ tight end room in routes since Ferguson went down, but his production has vanished over the past two weeks. Colby Parkinson scored in Week 6 and Davis Allen found the end zone twice last week. Higbee remains the best fantasy option of the bunch, but he’s nothing more than a low-end TE2 for Week 8.

Source: Gary Klein

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

There was hope within the organization late last week that Garrett could get back on the practice field today. That will have to wait at least one more week. Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 because of a knee issue that required surgery. His absence will make life for Jayden Daniels substantially easier in Week 8.

Source: Gary Klein

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Monday that St. Brown would likely miss today’s practice, so this isn’t much of a surprise. Campbell also told reporters that St. Brown “should be good” for Week 8, so we’re not panicking just yet. St. Brown is one of the few players who can suit up after missing an entire week of practice. Even a DNP tomorrow wouldn’t be the end of the world. For now, fantasy managers can treat St. Brown as a WR1, but a backup plan should be in place. Jameson Williams would vault into the WR1 ranks if St. Brown misses Week 8 versus the Vikings.

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Setting Brown’s drops aside, Brown still looked like he was working his way back from his high-ankle sprain last week against the Bears. He was laboring through his routes at times, particularly downfield. Targets should continue flowing his way, but Brown is perhaps best viewed as a volume-driven WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 8.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Carlton Davis (neck) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

Davis and both of the Patriots’ top perimeter backups, CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) are practicing in full this week. This is very good news. The trio has been sidelined for some time, weakening the Patriots’ secondary.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jahmyr Gibbs DET Running Back

A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

item.title: Jaylen Wright (foot/quad) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright is a mediocre bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon playing well in the lead role. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he may be able to slightly improve his efficiency if his health continues to improve.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Malik Washington (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Malik Washington MIA Wide Receiver

Washington has cooled off in recent weeks. Although his knee injury is unlikely to keep him out of the Dolphins’ Week 8 matchup against the Patriots, he is barely a WR5 in fantasy football. Washington does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Greg Dulcich (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Greg Dulcich MIA Tight End

The Dolphins’ tight end finally had a decent game, only to tweak an ankle along the way. He should be fine for Week 8 against the Patriots, but he is barely in the TE2 ranks.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Ravens claimed Christian Haynes off waivers from the Seahawks.
item.description:
Christian Haynes BAL Guard

Seattle cut the former third-round pick earlier this week after trading for Quenton Nelson. Haynes made five starts at right guard this year. Ravens rookie guard Vega Ioane is the latest in a long line of banged-up interior linemen for Baltimore. Haynes will give the team some extra depth.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell suffered the hip injury while logging a season-high 14 rush attempts in Week 7. The Bucs blew out the Panthers and racked up 49 carries as a team. Bucky Irving would be in line for more work on passing downs if Gainwell is out for Week 8. Sean Tucker could also see an uptick in snaps, though his normal role has very little overlap with what Gainwell does. Per usual, Irving looks like a high-end RB2 this week.

item.title: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

While we are happy to see Willis practicing in full, we are slightly unhappy to see that he has a new injury. The Dolphins’ quarterback has already dealt with toe and right thumb injuries this season. Willis remains a viable QB2 starter against the Patriots, but this is worth monitoring.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka logged one limited practice on Friday last week but was ruled out shortly after. It looks like he is trending in the right direction for Week 8, but the Bucs’ next two injury reports will be more revealing. Assuming all goes well, Egbuka should be back in the WR2 ranks with Baker Mayfield under center and playing well in Tampa Bay’s Week 7 demolition of the Panthers.

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase (NIR-rest/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

The rest aspect suggests Chase’s ankle injury can effectively be treated as a non-issue, but NFL teams have played games with the injury report at times this season, so we are cataloguing it here to be safe. Assuming Chase resumes practicing tomorrow, he can be started as an elite WR1, as usual, in Week 8 against the Titans.

Source: Jay Morrison

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

The hamstring issue is new, but it’s not one we expected to prevent Meyers from playing. A limited practice this early in the week is typically maintenance, especially midway through the season. Meyers will remains a fantasy WR4 for his Week 8 matchup with the Titans.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears had been playing through the knee issue for a few weeks before being sidelined because of it in Week 7. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Tony Pollard will handle the bulk of the backfield touches again this week. He remains a volume-based RB2 versus the Bengals.

item.title: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Olamide Zaccheaus ATL Wide Receiver

Zaccheaus’ shoulder injury caused him to miss the Falcons’ Week 7 game against the 49ers. Although he is not fantasy-relevant, his absence reduces the target competition for the remaining pass catchers.

Source: D. Orlando Ledbetter

item.title: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Bijan Robinson handled 20 carries and five targets with his backup, Brian Robinson, sidelined in Week 7. The backup should be considered questionable to play at this time, though he could make a late-week return. Stay tuned.

Source: D. Orlando Ledbetter

item.title: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

This is Warren’s first practice in two weeks, indicating he’s close to making a return. With Josh Downs failing to step up in his absence, the Colts desperately need Warren back in the lineup as their de facto WR1.
