The 28-year-old had a long rush of 16 yards, and the toe injury that sidelined him earlier in the campaign doesn’t appear to be bothering him. Dowdle is a FLEX option for Week 8 against the Browns, at best.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jaylen Warren rushed 18 times for 101 yards in the Steelers’ Week 7 win over the Saints, adding three catches for 36 yards.
item.description:
Jaylen Warren PIT Running Back

Warren got off to a hot start with 43 yards on the first drive, with 29 of those coming on a play that set up a short field goal. He totaled 78 yards in the first half, but found the sledding a little tougher in the final two periods with the Saints focused on stuffing the run. He outcarried Rico Dowdle 18-9, although Dowdle did add six catches to make the touches a little more even. Warren will look to impress again in Week 8 against the Browns’ front seven.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-38 passes for 273 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Saints’ 16-10, Week 7 loss to the Steelers.
item.description:
Tyler Shough NO Quarterback

Shough’s seven rushing yards led the team, which isn’t ideal. The 27-year-old was mostly accurate and on-time with his throws, but he should have had three turnovers on the first half — one dropped interception, one strip-sack that was overturned and one fumble that luckily went out of bounds — and he threw a costly red-zone interception. It wasn’t Shough at his best, but there were some flashes of brilliance in the loss. Shough will get a bye week before he faces the Browns in Week 9.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Aaron Rodgers completed 19-of-30 passes for 219 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ 16-10, Week 7 win over the Saints.
item.description:
Aaron Rodgers PIT Quarterback

Rodgers dinked and dunked for the overwhelming majority of the game with over half of his completions coming to his running backs. He did connect with DK Metcalf for a 51-yard connection on a beautiful deep ball, and he found Darnell Washington for his lone scoring play. Outside of that passing touchdown, the biggest play for Rodgers was a scramble on third-and-six just before the two-minute warning that essentially cemented the game. Rodgers and the Steelers move to 5-2 with the win in Paris, and they’ll face the Browns in Week 8. He’ll be a QB2 for that contest, on paper.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Za’Darius Smith (neck) and Gervon Dexter Sr. (hamstring) will both play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Za'Darius Smith ATL Defensive End

Both defenders were both listed as questionable for the Falcons, but both of them will be able to suit up, which is great news for the Falcons against a really banged-up 49ers offense. It remains to be seen if either player will play a full complement of snaps.

Source: Daniel Flick

item.title: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Olamide Zaccheaus ATL Wide Receiver

Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

Source: Daniel Flick

item.title: Denzel Ward (hand) is active for Week 7 against the Titans.
item.description:
Denzel Ward CLE Cornerback

Ward missed some practice time this week with a right hand injury. He’ll suit up against Cam Ward and the atrocious Titans passing attack. Browns declared QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, CB Noah Igbinoghene, RB Audric Estime, DT Mike Hall Jr., and C Parker Brailsford inactive against Tennessee.

item.title: 49ers declared DE Nick Bosa, WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, LB Luke Gifford, LB Garret Wallow, S Marques Sigle, and QB Kurtis Rourke inactive for Week 7 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

None of these comes as a surprise. All of Bosa, Evans, and Samuel were already ruled out earlier in the week, and Sigle has missed multiple weeks with an ankle injury. Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk are likely to lead the 49ers’ pass catchers against the Falcons this week, and both are worth adding in deeper formats in case either emerges as a legit weapon while Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are sidelined.

Source: Matt Barrows

item.title: Colts declared TE Tyler Warren, LB Bryce Boettcher, LB CJ Allen, CB Sauce Gardner, TE Tyler Warren, WR Anthony Gould, G Dalton Tucker, and QB Riley Leonard inactive for Week 7 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren was declared out earlier in the week due to a groin injury. Sauce Gardner (calf) and Anthony Gould (concussion) were also already declared out while Bryce Boettcher (groin) and CJ Allen (ankle) were declared out after having a questionable tag. Riley Leonard will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

item.title: Panthers declared EDGE Jaelan Phillips, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, C Sam Hecht, OT Stone Forsythe, and EDGE TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 7 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Jaelan Phillips CAR Outside Linebacker

Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

item.title: Dolphins declared WR Jalen Tolbert, LB Willie Gay, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., CB Reese Taylor, DE Rob Beal Jr., OL DJ Campbell, and OT Chukwuebuka Godrick inactive for Week 7 against the Jets.
item.description:
Jalen Tolbert MIA Wide Receiver

With Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell both healthy, Tolbert doesn’t have a spot on the game-day roster and is a healthy scratch this week. Douglas is back after missing a month because of an ankle injury.

item.title: Bengals declared S Russ Yeas, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, DE Shemar Stewart, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 7 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Shemar Stewart CIN Defensive End

The Bengals are coming off their bye at near-full strength, with all five inactives healthy scratches. Stewart, who was the No. 17 overall pick in last year’s draft, has appeared in just three games this season, totaling three tackles and one sack.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Theo Johnson (neck) is inactive for New York’s Week 7 game against the Texans.
item.description:
Theo Johnson NYG Tight End

Johnson was doubtful before being ruled out. He’ll have a chance to come back after New York’s Week 8 bye. Also inactive for the Giants are: OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow (knee), CB Greg Newsome II (concussion), S Jevón Holland (concussion), QB Jake Haener (3rd QB) and CB Nikko Reed. OT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and Tyler Nubin (neck) are playing despite being tagged as questionable on Friday.

item.title: Jordan Mason (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

The Vikings activated Mason off injured reserve and he is officially active for the first time since suffering a thumb injury in Week 1. He will split backfield touches with Aaron Jones, with Jones likely getting more of the passing-down work and Mason more the early-down work. Mason is a fantasy RB3 in his return. The Vikings declared S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, CB Chuck Demmings, RB Demond Claiborne, DL Elijah Willliams and OT Caleb Tiernan inactive for Week 7 against the Colts.

item.title: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, WR Elijah Sarratt, FS Jaylinn Hawkins, OG Andrew Vorhees, and DE Broderick Washington inactive for Week 7 against the Bengals
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Washington was the only player carrying a questionable designation heading into Sunday’s game, but he has officially been ruled out with an ankle injury. Jackson, who is also dealing with an ankle injury, will miss his third-straight game, paving the way for Tyler Huntley to start in the pivotal AFC North matchup.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

When last we left Mayfield, he was struggling mightily in Weeks 1-3. Predictably, UDFA Jalon Daniels was not any better in his stead. Mayfield returns to an undermanned skill corps, as Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) is out for Week 7. Mayfield is a shaky option in the QB16-18 range. Joining Egbuka on the shelf are OT Luke Goedeke, S Antoine Winfield, OG Billy Schrauth, DL DeMonte Capehart and CB Ayden Garnes.

item.title: Jets declared Breece Hall (quad) inactive for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Hall was reportedly unlikely to play as of this morning, so the news of his absence doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Braelon Allen will draw the start once again. Facing a dreadful Miami defense, Allen is on the RB1/2 border for Week 7. Also inactive for the Jets are CB Jarvis Brownlee, OG Dylan Parham, EDGE Joe Ossai, RB Kene Nwangwu, OG Max Mitchell, and DT Jack Heflin.

item.title: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Texans declared S Jalen Pitre (shoulder), RB David Montgomery (groin), S Reed Blankenship (concussion), T Blake Fisher (thumb), OL Febechi Nwaiwu, OL Nate Thomas and TE Marlin Klein inactive for Houston’s Week 7 game against the Giants.
item.description:
Jalen Pitre HOU Safety

Both Pitre and Montgomery, who are week-to-week, have a chance to come back after Houston’s Week 8 bye. They’ve both missed two weeks now with their respective injuries. The latter three are healthy scratches.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes the Jaguars “might be willing to listen” to trade offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Schefter didn’t directly cite any sources, but the dots are extremely easy to connect. Thomas Jr. has been the subject of trade rumors for the past year and his role has all but disappeared this season. He hasn’t caught a pass since Week 4 and was benched in the second half of the team’s Week 6 loss to Houston. At this point, a trade is seemingly in the best interest of both parties. Expect the market for Thomas Jr. to heat up ahead of the November 10th deadline.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined, life will not be easy for Tanner McKee on Monday evening, even in a plus matchup. Wicks drew some summer hype as a well-paid reclamation project for the Eagles, but he has caught more than three passes only two times all season and has not reached 70 yards since Week 2. He is a poor hold in 12-team leagues with five-man benches.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Peyton Manning is not expected to be a candidate for the Colts’ general manager vacancy.
item.description:
Peyton Manning

Manning was floated as a potential replacement for Chris Ballard after the latter was fired, but it was just baseless speculation. According to Schefter, the Colts have not discussed hiring Manning in any capacity. With no front office experience to his name and loads of media obligations to tend to, it doesn’t make sense for Manning to take a job with an NFL team at this time.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Alontae Taylor is expected to be active for Week 7 against the Browns.
item.description:
Alontae Taylor TEN Cornerback

Taylor, who was signed to a three-year, $60 million contract in the offseason, was a healthy scratch last week. That appears to be a temporary benching as Taylor will be back in the mix against Cleveland. Pro Football Focus currently has Taylor ranked 101st in coverage grade among all corners. His return doesn’t move the needle for Tennessee’s defense.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Washington (foot/back) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Rams.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Washington Jr. didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday but still received a questionable designation for Week 7. Fowler added that there is “some optimism” that he plays this week, but the pre-game workout will be the determining factor. Washington saw an uptick in carries last week with nine totes for 43 yards. We don’t expect as much work to go this way given the injury situation.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Grant Delpit (concussion) will play in Week 7 against the
item.description:
Grant Delpit CLE Safety

Delpit cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend and is good to go. Denzel Ward, on the other hand, will go through warmups to see if he can play. Ward is dealing with a hand injury and is listed as questionable for Week 7.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Budda Baker (groin/illness) is expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Budda Baker ARI Safety

Baker was listed as questionable for Week 7 after getting in a limited practice on Friday. He is good to go after making it through the weekend unscathed. Baker has one interception, four pass breakups, and a stunning 3.5 sacks this year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Nick Emmanwori (hip) is expected to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Nick Emmanwori SEA Safety

Uchenna Nwosu, also dealing with a hip injury, is also expected to suit up. No free lunch for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs this week. The Seahawks will be at full force. Facing the best defense in the league by most measures, Mahomes is on the QB1/2 border for Week 7.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Rapoport added that Jackson was really close to playing this week. With Tyler Huntley playing well enough to go 1-1 so far, the Ravens took a cautious approach and ruled him out for Week 7. Huntley will start versus the Bengals later today. If all goes well in practice next week, Jackson should be back and vying for the QB1 crown in a shootout with the Bills for Week 8.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are hopeful Myles Garrett (knee) returns to practice at least next week.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Rapoport didn’t go as far as to say they hope he is back for Week 8’s game against the Commanders, but it’s at least on the table. Garrett is currently on injured reserve, so we’ll know if he’s making progress if they open his practice window next week. The reigning DPOY has been out since Week 1 after undergoing surgery on his knee.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are “confident” Puka Nacua (calf) will play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua is going to test out his calf issue in warmups. Rapoport said Nacua isn’t necessarily dealing with a calf strain. He simply didn’t feel he could explode like he needed to. Nacua’s groin injury was described similarly earlier this year. Fantasy managers will want to keep an eye on this injury ahead of kickoff. If Nacua can’t go, Jordan Whittington will take on a larger role in the offense.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Josh Jacobs is expected to get “a normal allotment of reps for a starter” in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Packers OC Adam Stenavich told reporters Jacobs looked “great” in practice earlier this week, so we’re going to assume he’s in football shape and ready to go for Week 7. Given Garafolo’s reporting, Jacobs is already back on the RB1/2 border for a potential shootout with Detroit.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Za’Darius Smith (neck) is expected to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Za'Darius Smith ATL Defensive End

The same is true of Gervon Dexter, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Rapoport added that there is “much less optimism” for Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). That could mean an uptick in snaps for rookie wideout Zachariah Branch. He’s worth an add in deep leagues, but this offense isn’t likely to support another fantasy-relevant pass-catcher.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Pat Surtain (ankle) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Pat Surtain DEN Cornerback

Surtain will miss his third straight game with the ankle injury. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. With the Chiefs in the hole for Week 8, holding Surtain out one more game to get him back for a must-win AFC West showdown makes sense. Per Rapoport, there’s a “good chance” he’s back next week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Rico Dowdle (knee) is active for Week 7 against the Saints.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

The knee issue was new for Dowdle and limited him to three partial practices this week. He was listed as questionable for Week 7 on Friday. Dowdle will once again form the 1B portion of Pittsburgh’s backfield committee. He’s a low-end RB3 versus the Saints.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Rapoport added that Hall might work out to see if he can go, but it’s “a bit early” for him to return. That means he won’t be playing this week. Hall returned to practice on Wednesday but never got in a full session. The team will give him another week to ramp up. He should be back for Week 8 versus the Raiders. Braelon Allen will draw the start again this week, putting him near the top of the RB2 ranks versus Miami.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Giants are expected to start J.J. McCarthy “beyond their Week 8 bye.”
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

The Giants pivoted to “NINE” after he lit up the Saints for 243 yards in the fourth quarter of Week 6. Having already spent some draft capital to acquire McCarthy, the team is going to give him an extended tryout as the starter. If he does well, the Giants will likely hang on to him as Jaxson Dart’s backup next year. They could also trade him in the offseason if he plays well to garner interest from other teams.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cam Skattebo “is expected to resume his role as the team’s lead back” in Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Skattebo was benched for his fumbling issues last week. He did not touch the ball once, while Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy, and Devin Singletary all got a few opportunities. The team then cut Harris a few days after Sunday’s loss. After a week in the doghouse, Skattebo appears to be back as the team’s top runner, though we still expect a committee approach from John Harbaugh. Rapoport even said that it’s unclear who will draw the start, so we aren’t sold on Skattebo as a safe fantasy option this week. At best, he’s a high-risk RB3.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chiefs coach Andy Reid told Josh Simmons to leave a team meeting on Wednesday.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

According to Rapoport, Simmons was sitting with his feet up during a meeting and Reid told him to put his feet down. Simmons then “pushed back” by saying he had to sit that way because of his back injury. Reid then sent him to get treatment from the training staff. Even Patrick Mahomes chimed in and told Simmons to leave. Simmons was placed on injured reserve the next day. The former first-round pick appeared in just eight games as a rookie and hasn’t taken the field yet this year. Now he’s becoming a problem in the locker room on top of his never-ending health issues. We wouldn’t expect to see him play in a Chiefs uniform again anytime soon.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
Brian Branch DET Defensive Back

The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

item.title: Steelers declared CB Brandin Echols, WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Terell Smith inactive for Week 7 against the Saints.
item.description:
Brandin Echols PIT Cornerback

Echols and Skowronek are the only players on Pittsburgh’s active roster who will miss today’s game because of injuries, though they have several key players on IR. Both players have more snaps on special teams than offense or defense this year.

item.title: 49ers activated Christian Kirk (calf) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

The 49ers would normally have Kirk on a pitch count for his first game of the year. With their top four receivers unavailable for today’s game, Kirk may be thrust into a full-time role right away. He will be in the mix for WR1 duties in San Francisco alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. Kirk is a long-shot FLEX option for his first game as a 49er.

item.title: Browns signed Maliek Collins to a two-year, $30 million contract extension.
item.description:
Maliek Collins CLE Defensive Tackle

According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal includes $23 million in total guarantees. Collins has heated up recently with 3.5 sacks over his past three games. He is coming off a career-high 6.5 sacks in 2025 and now has a chance to top that number this year. Collins’ new deal keeps him under contract with the Browns through 2028.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Saints declared OG Cesar Ruiz, S Mike Reid, TE Treyton Welch, EDGE Tyree Wilson, DL Nathan Shepherd, DT John Ridgeway III, and QB Zach Wilson inactive for Week 7 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Cesar Ruiz NO OFFENSIVE GUARD (SUB)

Ruiz and Shepard were the only Saints listed as questionable for Week 7. Jeremiah Wright will take his spot at right guard.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Although getting in a full practice Saturday, the Eagles head into Monday’s game against the Cowboys with Barkley listed as questionable following a two-game absence. Fantasy managers have a decision considering the Eagles play in Week 7’s final game on Monday Night Football, with no clear fall back options should he be unable to play. It would seem prudent to make alternate plans at the position.

item.title: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Browns activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

Sampson was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable for Week 7 against the Titans. Now that he’s officially been activated from injured reserve, he’s likely to be Cleveland’s change-of-pace back behind Quinshon Judkins this week. Sampson is worth stashing on fantasy benches, but is truly just a desperation FLEX play coming off a knee injury that’s sidelined him since Week 1.

Source: Fred Greetham

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that several teams believe the Jaguars could trade WR Brian Thomas Jr.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler, citing Thomas’ zero catches over the last two weeks, said something has to give in this situation. According to several teams the NFL Insider talked to, Thomas could be traded over the next few weeks. Fowler listed the Chiefs and Steelers as potentially interested teams and was emphatic that there will be suitors for Thomas. If you have Thomas in fantasy, it’s hard to imagine his value getting worse with a change of scenery. The Jaguars would appear content to roll with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter as their top receivers in the event of a Thomas trade.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

Source: Joanthan Jones

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Colts aren’t discussing a Jonathan Taylor trade yet.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Jones writes that his understanding is the Colts will wait a few weeks before deciding what to do with their star running back. Indianapolis decided to move on from GM Chris Ballard after a 2-4 start. The way things are trending, it’s easy to imagine the Colts still on the outside of the playoff race in a few weeks. At that point interim GM Ed Dodds could look to recoup draft assets the team lost in previous trades. According to Jones, moving Taylor “would be the most expedient route” to acquiring a high draft pick. Citing sources, Jones lists the Giants and Vikings as potential suitors if Taylor is made available on the trade market. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August that hasn’t even kicked in yet.

Source: Jonathan Jones

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is “50/50" to play against the Bengals in Week 7.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler said the Ravens are “hopeful” that Jackson can play against the Bengals. He added that the team isn’t “overly optimistic” because, according to a source, Jackson is “50/50" to play in Week 7. If Jackson can’t go, Tyler Huntley will get the start and fantasy managers will need a backup plan this week. At this point, it’s unlikely we receive more clarity on the situation before inactives are released Sunday morning.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

Source: Colton Pouncy

item.title: Jevón Holland (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Jevón Holland NYG Safety

Holland, the Giants’ starting free safety, and Tyler Nubin (neck), the Giants’ starting strong safety, are both questionable to play. Meanwhile, starting perimeter CB Greg Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out. Expect the Texans’ passing offense to stay hot this week.

Source: New York Giants

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (hip) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

The Seahawks’ sporadic producer will be on the field against the Chiefs this week. Shaheed has been involved as a receiver and as a rusher, scoring touchdowns in consecutive weeks. He offers a low floor, but he makes for a viable FLEX starter this week.

Source: Seattle Seahawks

item.title: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Landon Dickerson PHI Guard

Dickerson injured a pectoral muscle on Thursday, complicating his knee-related return from injured reserve. He is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was upgraded to full participation.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

We had really hoped to see Barkley practice in full today. He still has a chance to take the field when the Eagles face the Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, but he is inching toward a questionable designation right now. Upgrading to full tomorrow would increase his odds of playing.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks has been banged up for weeks, and the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said Wicks might miss the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow. Stay tuned.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said he got “the sense” that DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Like Thursday, Smith was sidelined for Friday’s practice. The Eagles have been managing his practice reps and pulled him out for multiple drives in their Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night, giving Smith an extra day to rest. Consider him highly questionable to play at this time. McLane adds that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could also sit out this week.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Kendal Daniels (neck) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Kendal Daniels ATL Linebacker

Daniels was taken off the field on a stretcher last week, but managed to practice in full to begin the week. Daniels, a rookie, has 23 tackles, three quarterback pressures and one sack this season.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: A.J. Terrell (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
A.J. Terrell ATL Cornerback

Both Terrell and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) are questionable to play after practicing in full on Friday. Getting them back in the starting lineup would be very helpful for the Falcons’ defense.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Budda Baker ARI Safety

Baker practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, and the veteran safety is no stranger to playing through injuries. The Cardinals ruled out DL Walter Nolen (ankle) and S Andrew Wingard (knee). Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) has been cleared to play.

Source: Darren Urban

item.title: Broncos ruled out Jonah Elliss (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jonah Elliss DEN Linebacker

Reporting from earlier this week indicates Ellis could be sidelined for a few weeks. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was also ruled out this week.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Pat Surtain (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Pat Surtain DEN Cornerback

Surtain never managed to practice in full this week. Keeping him sidelined until he is able to do so could make sense. The 4-2 Broncos are currently second in the AFC West. They face the 5-0 Chiefs in Week 8. Stay tuned.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Broncos ruled out Tyler Badie (thumb) for Week 7
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

Badie is likely headed toward a demotion with Jonah Coleman (ankle) inching toward a return. The latter player is questionable to play this week.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle upgraded to full on Friday after logging two limited sessions to begin the week. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver has struggled to deliver usable stat lines with Bo Nix intent on checking down. The Cardinals’ pass defense could facilitate a bounce-back game for Waddle, but he remains a WR3/FLEX at this time.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Drew Lock (right elbow) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks’ backup quarterback is dealing with an injury in his throwing arm, so any calls for Sam Darnold’s benching will have to quiet down. Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) are questionable. The Seahawks ruled out Chazz Surratt (calf) and LB DrakeThomas (ankle).

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Vikings released RB Deejay Dallas.
item.description:
DeeJay Dallas MIN Running Back

He’ll likely find his way back to the practice squad — here or elsewhere — at some point this season. This move portends that Jordan Mason will be activated for Week 7.

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus after being activated from injured reserve Saturday.

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

The 49ers keep projecting a rosy picture of Bosa returning to practice at some point, it keeps not happening. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. Bosa hasn’t played since Week 2. If only there were a reserve list that teams could place injured players on.

item.title: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
item.description:
KaVontae Turpin DAL Wide Receiver

Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

item.title: Falcons activated A.J. Terrell (groin) from injured reserve.
item.description:
A.J. Terrell ATL Cornerback

The Falcons have been attackable on the perimeter while playing most of the season without Terrell. Fellow cornerback C.J. Henderson is listed questionable for Week 7, but the reintegration of Terrell provides a much more difficult matchup for the injury-riddled 49ers.

item.title: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

item.title: Ravens ruled out Lamar Jackson (ankle) for Week 7 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Tyler Huntley will draw the start under center for the third straight game as Jackson continues to rehab a high-ankle sprain. Jackson reportedly took most of the first-team reps at practice Friday and was close to being able to play in Week 7, with the team ultimately siding with caution for their franchise quarterback. The Ravens enter a 15-game stretch in which they play three games starting in Week 8, which could have influenced their decision to hold Jackson out one more game. Expect him back for Week 8 against the Bills. His absence greatly influences the upside of the remaining skill position players considering Declan Doyle has halved his usage of play action and completely eliminated RPO with Huntley under center.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

item.title: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel hasn’t practiced since injuring his hamstring in the latter stages of Week 5’s win over the Seahawks. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. It does seem like there’s at least some chance he could get active for Week 9.

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice all week and will get San Francisco’s Week 8 bye to recover. The 33-year-old’s absence will leave veterans Christian Kirk and Brandin Cooks along with youngsters Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins on the 49ers receiver depth chart for Sunday.

item.title: Tyler Guyton (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Tyler Guyton DAL Tackle

This is great news for the Cowboys’ offense. Guyton, the starting left tackle, is practicing in full and still has another practice tomorrow. Expect him to be available for the Cowboys’ Monday Night Football game against the Eagles.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Trent Brown (wrist) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Trent Brown HOU Tackle

He’ll be good to go after back-to-back full sessions on Thursday and Friday. The 380-pound behemoth will likely continue to spend plenty of time on the injury report in his age-33 season.

item.title: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

Source: Jon Machota

item.title: Matthew Golden (shoulder) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

A few Packers got a little banged up against the Cowboys last week, including Golden, but the breakout second-year wide receiver is good to go. This game profiles as a fantasy-friendly shootout. Golden should be started as a high-end WR2 with solid upside.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) is not on Las Vegas’ final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

A Friday afternoon tradition unlike any other, Bowers was cleared after getting in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. He can be played as an elite TE1, as usual.

item.title: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) will miss the remainder of the season.
item.description:
Tremaine Edmunds NYG Linebacker

Edmunds will presumably be placed on IR before Week 7’s game against the Texans. He managed a 52.0 PFF grade in 380 snaps over six games, recording two sacks and 50 combined tackles. Edmunds will enter year two of his three-year deal with the Giants in 2027, in what will be his age-29 season.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Theo Johnson (neck) is doubtful for Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Theo Johnson NYG Tight End

Johnson is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but he can help out the Giants’ offense in real life when he is available. Isaiah Likely is the Giants’ clear-cut TE1.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas has played through injuries in multiple games this year. Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) both resumed practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and are officially questionable to play this week. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year. Perhaps this is a get-right matchup for them.

Source: Art Stapleton

item.title: Brian Branch (Achilles) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Brian Branch DET Defensive Back

After three full sessions this week, Branch is expected to be activated off reserve/PUP and should have no snap count per DC Kelvin Sheppard. He can be welcomed back to IDP lineups.

item.title: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on Kansas City’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

He’ll be a reliable TE1, even in a tough matchup against Seattle’s defense, as the Chiefs simply don’t have many other Trusted Mahomes Targets healthy for this one. It’s essentially just Kelce and Xavier Worthy healthy of Kansas City’s main targets.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears has been active off a questionable line twice since Week 4. We’d imagine he’d get there again after a limited Friday session. The touch upside just isn’t there for him to be more than a deep-league FLEX play at this point.

item.title: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters earlier today that Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go” for this week’s game. Mayfield seemingly has solid odds of suiting up this week, but we must wait for an official ruling. Hopefully, that arrives tomorrow. If active, Mayfield will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help keep his recently dislocated thumb in place. He is a QB2 for the occasion, if active.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday, and we’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Not that you were thinking about playing him anyway.

item.title: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Ashton Dulin IND Wide Receiver

With Tyler Warren down, Dulin probably figures to join Keenan Allen and Josh Downs as one of Indianapolis’ three main receivers. He has some desperation play viability in deeper leagues.

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight will handle “a lot of work” on early downs with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

LaFleur simply does not believe that any one running back can handle a full-time role and remain healthy, so he employs a committee approach. Although Tyler Allgeier sits ahead of Knight on the depth chart, LaFleur said he views Allgeier as a reliable complementary running back who excels in pass protection and short-yardage. Knight will be the team’s lead rusher on early downs and can be started in the FLEX against the Broncos this week.

Source: Tyler Drake

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Tyler Allgeier is “always” going to serve as a complementary running back.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

LaFleur really laid it all out there at today’s press conference, saying Allgeier “is always going to complement that next guy” when the starter is out. He adds that Allgeier is “extremely smart” and can be trusted in pass protection and short-yardage situations on third down. While Allgeier “can” do what the Cardinals need him to do on first and second down, LaFleur said Bam Knight will take “a lot” of that work with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined. LaFleur closed by saying he does not think any of these running backs can hold up in a full-time role over the course of the season. Allgeier handled a hefty 19 touches in this complementary role last week. He can be started as a high-volume FLEX with touchdown-based upside against the Broncos.

Source: Tyler Drake

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

He is, however, expected to be activated off injured reserve and play. We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus assuming he is indeed activated on Saturday.

item.title: GeorgePickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

Source: Jon Machota

item.title: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie has not practiced since straining his groin in Week 6’s Thursday practice. Labeling him as questionable to play seems like a formality before a game-day inactive listing, but only the Rams’ staffers know for sure. The Rams ruled out LB Nate Landman (concussion). Practice squad LB Eric Kendricks will be promoted to the active roster for Week 7.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

The fact that Nacua is not practicing today is a bad sign for his Week 7 availability. Ever the injury-related optimist, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier today that Nacua’s injury is “more minor than anything else,” though he quickly balanced the scales by then saying that he would not call Nacua’s quick trip to the imaging room “precautionary, because it’s not nothing.” If active, Nacua should be in fantasy football lineups because his talent and workload are almost unparalleled. Unfortunately, coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua felt that “he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion.” Nacua is on the wrong side of questionable, and the Rams obviously do not want his injury to worsen.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Brashard Smith (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Brashard Smith KC Running Back

Did you remember he was on the roster? Funny what one little Kenneth Walker signing will do. Smith has one touch and six snaps in five games. Jadyn Ott will get RB3 duties in Week 7.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) is not on the Vikings’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and was able to heal up over the Vikings’ Week 6. He demonstrated a solid connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, posting a 13/119 receiving line against the Dolphins. Hockenson can be treated as a TE1 this week against the Colts.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice didn’t practice all week despite Andy Reid’s optimistic spin that he’s a “quick healer.” It’s hard to make much sense of how available he’ll be for Week 8 at this point as Rice hasn’t practiced since before the team’s Week 5 bye. Xavier Worthy will again get a WR3-caliber workload as The Only Game In Town for the Chiefs wideouts.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday. The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Cole Kmet (knee) will miss the rest of the season.
item.description:
Cole Kmet CHI Tight End

Unfortunately it’s not much of a surprise based on the reporting or the carting. Sam Roush will take over as Chicago’s TE2 and likely have fringe TE2 value. Kmet will be in the final year of his four-year, $50 million extension in 2027. The 28-year-old will be a potential cap casualty with a $15.425 million cap figure and $10 million in savings on release without getting into post-June 1 cap machinations.

Source: Phillip Thompson

item.title: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

Source: Alec Lewis
